incident_findings: The first exhausted task attempt emitted invalid JSON syntax and has no unique executable interpretation.
The second attempt emitted valid JSON with exactly one allow-listed dynamic tool-name key equal to its own string value plus an unchanged arguments object.
Reply policy v3 rejected the second shape even though its mapping to canonical name and arguments is unique.
No R4 reward, task success, expected action, or formal gold was used to define the mapping.

accepted_shape.arguments: must be an object and is copied without mutation

rejected_shapes: dynamic value different from the dynamic key

no_model_acceptance.positive_fixture: accepted and mapped to the identical allow-listed name and unchanged arguments object
no_model_acceptance.legacy_v3_fixture: same shape remains rejected under explicit v3 policy

acceptance_basis: The rule performs no JSON repair, tool-name inference, argument synthesis, or argument mutation.
The exact per-turn allow-list remains authoritative before any executable call can leave the adapter.
The policy is explicitly bound through the formal protocol, child environment, runtime config, composition digest, and evidence records.
R4 remains immutable and a new experiment must symmetrically rerun all 25 Update-Source positions.
limitations: The no-model fixtures prove the transformation and fail-closed boundaries, not provider frequency or task quality.
Malformed JSON remains Infra Invalid after the frozen retry budget is exhausted.
The R5 paid symmetric rerun is required before this policy can support any downstream candidate claim.
Local compute monetary cost remains unmetered; process time and memory must be reported separately.
